newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi says has no illegal 'tobashi' deals.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi says has no illegal 'tobashi' deals.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd chairman Tsugio Yukihira said on Wednesday that his company had no illegal "tobashi" deals.
A tobashi deal is one in which brokers seek to hide a client's investment losses by transferring them to another client.
Japanese media reported in the past month that Yamaichi, Japan's fourth-biggest securities house, had carried out such deals.
Yukihira is also the acting chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA).

Asked at a JSDA press conference about media reports of Yamaichi tobashi deals worth 400 billion yen, Yukihira said: "I would like to decline to comment, as I am acting chairman of this association, but because this matter relates to confidence in the industry, I must say that we don't have any such deals at all."
Yukihira declined to comment on questions about Yamaichi's reported move to merge some of its affiliated brokers.

Earlier on Wednesday, a Yamaichi spokesman said one option for helping the company's affiliated brokerages would be to merge them into one entity. He said the firm would decide on steps to aid its affiliates as soon as possible.
At the Wednesday afternoon news conference, Yukihira said that if there were merits or advantages for brokers to restructure themselves, then they would take such action.
